====================================================================================================
TEXT #1
====================================================================================================

These spiced salts are used against indigestion, to move the bowels, against all illness, against
pestilence as well as for the prevention of colds. They are very gentle indeed and more healthful
than you would expect. [tor. Make them in this manner]: 1 lb. Of common salt ground, 2 lbs. Of
ammoniac salt, ground [list. And g.-v. 3 ozs. White pepper, 2 ozs. Ginger] 1 oz. [tor. 1 oz.] of
aminean bryony, 1 of thyme seed and 1 of celery seed [tor. 1 oz.] if you don t want to use celery
seed take instead 3 ozs. Of parsley [seed] 3 ozs. Of origany, 1 oz. Of saffron [list. And g.-v.
Rocket] 3 ozs. Of black pepper [1] 1 ozs. Rocket seed, 2 ozs. Of marjoram [list. And g.-v. Cretan
hyssop] 2 ozs. Of nard leaves, 2 ozs. Of parsley [seed] and 2 ozs. Of anise seed.

====================================================================================================
TEXT #2
====================================================================================================

Soak [pignolia] nuts, dry them, and also have fresh sea-urchins [1] ready. Take a deep dish
[casserole] in which arrange the following things [in layers]: medium-sized mallows and beets,
mature leeks, celery, stewed tender green cabbage, and other boiled green vegetables [2], a
disjointed [3] chicken stewed in its own gravy, cooked [calf s or pig s] brains, lucanian sausage,
hard boiled eggs cut into halves, big tarentinian sausage [4] sliced and broiled in the ashes,
chicken giblets or pieces of chicken meat. Bits of fried fish, sea nettles, pieces of [stewed]
oysters and fresh cheese are alternately put together; sprinkle in between the nuts and whole
pepper, and the juice as is cooked from pepper, lovage, celery seed and silphium. This essence, when
done, mix with milk to which raw eggs have been added [pour [102] this over the pieces of food in
the dish] so that the whole is thoroughly combined, stiffen it [in the hot water bath] and when done
[garnish with] fresh mussels [sea-urchins, poached and chopped fine] sprinkle pepper over and serve.

====================================================================================================
TEXT #3
====================================================================================================

The apician dish is made thus: take small pieces of cooked sow s belly [with the paps on it] pieces
of fish, pieces of chicken, the breasts of figpeckers or of thrushes [slightly] cooked, [and]
whichever is best. Mince all this very carefully, particularly the figpeckers [the meat of which is
very tender]. Dissolve in oil strictly fresh eggs; crush pepper and lovage, pour over some broth and
raisin wine, put it in a saucepan to heat and bind with roux. After you have cut all in regular
pieces, let it come to the boiling point. When done, retire [from the fire] with its juice of which
you put some in another deep pan with whole pepper and pignolia nuts. Spread [the ragout] out in
single layers with thin pancakes in between; put in as many pancakes and layers of meat as is
required to fill the dish; put a final cover of pancake on top and sprinkle with pepper after those
eggs have been added [which serve] to tie the dish. Now put this [mould or dish] in a boiler
[steamer, hot water bath, allow to congeal] and dish it out [by unmoulding it]. An expensive silver
platter would enhance the appearance of this dish materially.

====================================================================================================
TEXT #4
====================================================================================================

The moveable [1] appetizers are thus made: [2] small white beets, mature leeks, celery roots [3]
stewed cockles [4] ginger [5] chicken giblets, small fowl [6] small morsels cooked in their own
liquor [7]. Oil a pan, line it with mallow leaves and a composition of different vegetables, and, if
you have room enough, bulbs, damascus plums, snails, tid-bits [8] short lucanian sausage sliced; add
broth, oil, wine, vinegar put on the fire to heat and so cook them. Meanwhile crush pepper, lovage,
ginger, a little tarragon, moisten it and let it cook. Break several eggs in a dish, use the
remaining liquor in the mortar to mix it with the sauce in the dish and to bind it. When this is
done, make a wine sauce for it as follows: crush pepper, lovage, moistened with broth, raisin wine
to taste; in a small sauce pan put a little oil [with the other ingredients] heat, and bind with
roux when hot. Now [unmould] upset the dish on a platter, remove the mallow leaves, pour over the
wine sauce, sprinkle with pepper and serve [9].

====================================================================================================
TEXT #5
====================================================================================================

A dish of stuffed pumpkin [1] is made thus: [2] peel and cut the pumpkin lengthwise into oblong
pieces which hollow out and put in a cool place. The dressing for the same make in this way: crush
pepper, lovage and origany, moistened with broth; mince cooked brains and beat raw eggs and mix all
together to form a paste; add broth as taste requires. Stuff the above prepared pieces of pumpkin
that have not been fully cooked with the dressing; fit two pieces together and close them tight
[holding them by means of strings or skewers]. [now poach them and] take the cooked ones out and fry
them [3]. [the proper] wine sauce [for this dish] make thus: crush pepper, lovage moistened with
wine, raisin wine to [121] taste, a little oil, place in pan to be cooked; when done bind with roux.
Cover the fried pumpkin with this sauce, sprinkle with pepper and serve [4].

====================================================================================================
TEXT #6
====================================================================================================

Cook the peas with oil and a piece of sow s belly [2] put in a sauce pan broth, leek heads [the
lower white part] green coriander and put on the fire to be cooked. Of tid-bits [3] cut little dice.
Similarly cook thrushes or other small [game] birds, or take sliced chicken and diced brain,
properly cooked. Further cook, in the available liquor or broth, lucanian sausage and bacon; cook
leeks in water; crush a pint of toasted pignolia nuts; also crush pepper, lovage, origany and
ginger, dilute with the broth of pork, tie [4] take a square baking dish suitable for turning over
which oil well and line with caul [5] sprinkle [on the bottom] a layer of crushed nuts upon which
put some peas, fully covering the bottom of the squash dish; on top of this arrange slices of the
bacon [6] leeks and sliced lucanian sausage; again cover with a layer of peas and alternate all the
rest of the available edibles in the manner described until the dish is filled, concluding at last
with a layer of peas, utilizing everything. Bake this dish in the oven, or put it into a slow fire
[covering it with live coal] so that it may be baked thoroughly. [next make a sauce of the
following] put yolks of hard boiled eggs in the mortar with white pepper, nuts, honey, white wine
and a little broth; mix and put it into a sauce pan to be cooked; when [the sauce is] done, turn out
the peas into a large [silver dish] and mask them with this sauce which is called white sauce [7].

====================================================================================================
TEXT #7
====================================================================================================

Bone [either] chicken [or suckling pig] from the chicken remove the breast bone and the [upper joint
bones of the] legs; hold it together by means of wooden skewers, and meanwhile [2] prepare [the
following dressing in this manner]: alternate [inside of the chicken or pig] peas with the pods
[washed and cooked], brains, lucanian sausage, etc. Now crush pepper, lovage, origany and ginger,
moistened with broth, raisin wine and wine to taste, make it boil, when done, use it moderately for
seasoning and alternately with the other dressing; wrap [the chicken, or pig] in caul, place it in a
baking dish and put it in the oven to be cooked slowly, and serve.

====================================================================================================
TEXT #8
====================================================================================================

Cook the chicken [as follows, in] broth, oil, with wine added, to which add a bunch of coriander and
[green] onions. When done take it out [3] [strain and save] the broth, and put it in a new sauce
pan, add milk and a little salt, honey and a pint [4] of water, that is, a third part: place it back
on a slow fire to simmer. Finally break [the paste, [1]] put it little by little into [the boiling
broth] stirring well so it will not burn. Put the chicken in, either whole or in pieces [5] dish it
out in a deep dish. This cover with the following sauce [6] pepper, lovage, origany, moistened with
honey and a little reduced must. Add some of the [chicken] broth, heat in a small sauce pan and when
it boils thicken with roux [7] and serve.

====================================================================================================
TEXT #9
====================================================================================================

Clean the paunch of a suckling pig well with salt and vinegar and presently wash with water. Then
fill it with the following dressing: pieces of pork pounded in the mortar, three brains the nerves
removed mix with raw eggs, add nuts, whole pepper, and sauce to taste. Crush pepper, lovage,
silphium, anise, ginger, a little rue; fill the paunch with it, not too much, though, leaving plenty
of room for expansion lest it bursts while being cooked. Put it in a pot with boiling water, retire
and prick with a needle so that it does not burst. When half done, take it out and hang it into the
smoke to take on color; now boil it over again and finish it leisurely. Next take the broth, some
pure wine and a little oil, open the paunch with a small knife. Sprinkle with the broth and lovage;
place the pig near the fire to heat it, turn it around in bran [or bread crumbs] immerse in
[sprinkle with] brine and finish [the outer crust to a golden brown] [1].

TEXT #10
====================================================================================================

Pepper, lovage, syrian sumach, dry mint, rue berries, hard yolks, mead, vinegar, broth, oil; cook
it. End of book x the last of the books of apicius celii apitii halieus liber decimus & ultimus.
Explicit [tac.] cantharus, wine bowl or cup with elaborate ornamentation: over a sacred fountain the
walls of a theatre, with emblems of a theatrical nature and garlands of flowers and fruits, wine
skins, tyrsus, torches, masks and musical instruments. Hildesheim treasure. [232] opening chapter,
book i, venice, 1503 from the lancilotus edition, printed by tacuinus in venice in 1503. Identical
with the two previous editions except for very minor variants. The rubrication is not completed
here. Fine initials were painted in the vacant spaces by hand; the small letter in the center of the
square being the cue for the rubricator. This practice, a remnant from the manuscript books, was
very soon abandoned after the printing of books became commercialized. [233]

schwaer auf die pleter (pancake) vnd lass ain nacht dar vnnder ligen so werden sy hert vnd kalt das
sol von zucker (unrefined cane sugar) sues sein . So machst du es sue geben. Wann du wild vnd behalt
es wie lanng du wild oder wann du es geben wild so nymm ain scharpffs messer (knife) vnd schneids
wie du wild vnd legs vf ain schuessel (bowl) so [29v] sichstu die farb (food coloring) gar das ist

sein die suellen vnd woellen froelich sein das sol geschehen vor dem tisch (table) da sicht man den
tiergarten her gen darinne sind man vnd frauen vnd iunckfrawen auch ain tail wann er sein nicht
gelauben wil der mags wol sehen wann es kumpt fuer den tisch (table) so mag man es wol gesehen . Vnd
das wist darinne sind auch schueczen vnd waeppner vnd annder kurczweilig ding das man darinne koech
vindet so sicht man die purg vnndergann so wirt das thor auf gethan so sich man die bischoff her
fuer gann vnd den koch darunder stan der das feur (ember) dar ein hat gethan nider laet er gann auf
die pannck vnd zeuecht ein kopff zue hannd aus dem laet man im geben vnd ze hannt wider auf den
tisch (table) [108v] darinne sind zwaierlaj vogel (bird) das suellen wissen vnd wann sy nit
annderlaj haben gasz so fliegen die anndern von stat . So sich ich den affen gen in dem tiergarten .
Vnd das ist ein etc. Woellend sy mer essen so gib gepachen visch (fish) vnd gesoten vnd gepraten
etc. Also hastu guot ding von allerlay kochen von maister hannsen des von wirtenberg koch etc.

dem fewer (ember) vnd bezeuch den appfel (apple) halben mit einem totter (yolk) als vil dw wild vnd
ein wenig auf dy anderen seytten dye totteren (yolk) mit dem gruen saft aus petersil (parsley juice)
vnd stoz in ein mosrer (mortar) vnd leg in dan darnach auf ein tuech (cheesecloth) vnd twing in

seytten mit dem gruen totteren (yolk) so ist beraytt

Welt ir haben ain ckerssen (sour cherry) tranck (drink) so nempt czeytig weyssel (sour cherry) sewd
dy vnd slags durch czwier oder treystundt lass woll gessen vnd lass ligen vncz das lessen kumpt so
nym [81v] suessen most (fruit juice) sewd das laz in vergessen geus dar in so beleib er bey seiner
varib (food coloring) will dw das tranck (drink) guett haben so tue ingwer (ginger) galgant (lesser
galangal) tandel (unsolved) czyment (cinnamon) vnd peyll (unsolved) vnd vermachs woll vnd nagel
(clove) in ain sackel (bag) vnd henck das hin ein czw dem peyll (unsolved) vnd vermachs woll wurd es
czestarck so nym das sackel (bag) her au vnd trucken es pey dem offen (baking oven) vnde duodecimade
mensis etc.

Item will dw machen ein spansaw (suckling pig) in einer leber (calf liver) sulcz (aspic) so nym
czway taill wein (wine) vnd ain taill wasser (water) vnd sewd dy spensaw (suckling pig) vnd ainer
kelbrenn leber (calf liver) da pey / vnd wen es nun gesotten sey so seich dy prue (liver suckling
pig broth) ab vnd stoz dy leber (calf liver) in ainem morsar (mortar) vnd nym ainer patten semell
(white bread) vnd iiij ayr tutter (yolk) thue dy auch vntter dy leber (calf liver) vnd streichs dan
in der prue (liver suckling pig broth) durch da sy inn gesotten ist vnd nyms in phann (pan) erbells
machs mit saffrann (saffron) vnd mit guetten gwurcz (spice) geuss dan vber dy spensaw (suckling pig)
in we dw sey dan gelegt hast es sey schussel (bowl) oder ckaren (container) etc.

Ain guette salsen (sauce) accipe folia piretri (pellitory) munda et laua in aqua (water) mundissima
et lota experime aquam fortissime (nitric acid) postea pone in vase () mundo et super effunde acetum
(vinegar) bonum ita vt acetum (vinegar) super eminet herbis (pellitory) et mitte stare pro diem
naturalem post hoc experime ecetum (vinegar) ab herbe (pellitory) fortiter et tandem in cide
minutissime in modum pulueris et exhinc pone in patellam (container) mundam et exquoque cum melle
(nectar) prius dispunnato et ista dispunacio habet fieri in modum sicut lebetary faciunt lebetis et
excoccio debet fieri ad vnam horam continue cum spatula lignea (spatula) mouendo et vltram bulicione
in pone pulueres pipperum (pepper) et hoc habitis salsamenta (fish sauce) optima etc.

Ein gebraten gefueltez ferhelin (suckling pig) . Ein gebraten gefultez ferhelin (suckling pig) mache
also nim ein verkelin (suckling pig) daz drier wuochen alt si . Vnd brue daz kuele . Vnd zuehe im
daz har (hair) allez abe daz man ez iht wunde . So sol man im vemme den rans vssene die hut (pork
rind) lazzen . Vnd loese beide fleisch (pork) . Vnd gebeine (bone) abe . Vnd allez daz ez in dem
libe hat . An die klawen die ez nidennen hat . Vf den fuezzen . Vnd nime des fleisches (pork) daz
dor vz gezogen ist wol als zwei eier (chicken egg) vnd suede ez vilnach gar . Vnd nime danne daz .
Vnd spec (bacon) vnd hackez . Tuo rowe eyer (chicken egg) dor zvo vnd eine sniten broetes (bread)
vnd peterlin krut (parsley) . Vnd saltz (table salt) zvo mazze . Vnd fuelle da mit daz ferkelin
(suckling pig) niht alzv vol vnd forne den munt (pig's snout) vnd legez sanfte in einen kezzel
(cauldron) laz ez erwallen [157r] daz die hut (pork rind) iht zvo breche . So nim ez denne . Vnd
lege ez vf einen huelzinen roest (wooden grate) vnd brate ez sanfte alz ez denne wol geroest si so
nim ein bret (cutting board) vnd lege daz vf eine schuezzeln (bowl) mache vf daz bret (cutting
board) vier steckelin (rod) vn cleide daz bret (cutting board) mit eime blat (pancake) von eyern
(chicken egg) . Vnd setze das verkelin (suckling pig) dar vf . Cleide ez auch mit eime blate
(pancake) vnd laz im die oeren (pig's ear) darvz gen vnd den munt (pig's snout) vnde trage ez hin .

vnd decke ez mit eyme duennen teyge (dough) vnd mache daz vmeme vnd vem . Gantz vnd brich oben ein
loch dor in vnd lege da fuer ein cluesterlin von teyge (dough) vnd laz ez backen . Also mac man auch

im die hut (stockfish skin) abe weich in in kaltem wazzer (water) eine naht vnd nim denne hervz vnd

laze in wol belaufen mit butern (butter) dor noch mache einen schoenen teyk (dough) mit wizzem melwe
(wheat flour) . Vnd mit eyern (chicken egg) dor zvo tuo gestozzen pfeffer (pepper) oder ingeber
(ginger) vnd ein wenic saffrans (saffron) saltz (table salt) zvo mazze sprengez vf den visch
(stockfish) als der visch (stockfish) gar heiz si so slahe den teyg (dough) dor vf mit eime swanke .

veizt mit butern (butter) . Vnd gib in hin .

Ein guot spise . Nim gesotene swins darme (pig intestine) vnd den magen (pig's stomach) snit die
gesoten darm (pig intestine) in viere die langen vnd die cleinen dar nach snides gefuege als die
riemen vnd den magen (pig's stomach) snide auch smal vnd snit denne beide magen (pig's stomach) vnd
darm (pig intestine) den ietweders veber so du cleinest wilt . Nim petersilien (parsley) bolei
(pennyroyal) vnd minzzen (mint) . Salbey (common sage) gesotene herte eyer (chicken egg) vnd schoene
brot (bread) kuemels (caraway) aller meist vnd ein wenic pfeffers (pepper) vnd ein ey (chicken egg)
zvo der schuezzeln (bowl) idiz male mit ezzige (vinegar) vnd mit guoteme sode (stock) also daz ez
niht zesur werde vnd guez ez vf die kaldiment (tripe) vnd tuo smaltz (lard) dor zvo laz ez erwarmen
vntz ez dicke werde gibz hin vnd versaltz niht .

von flemen daz tuo die wile ez vngesoten ist als lanc vnd groz als die darm (pig intestine) sint

verbint beide die innern vnd den grozzen darm (intestine) an beiden enden besunder . Teil daz
condiment (sauce) glich in die darm (intestine) suet sie gar vnd gib sie heyz hin

Ein guot spise nim von der brust des huones (chicken breast) vnd hacke ez cleine vnd stoz ez in eime
moerser (mortar) . Vnd tuo dar zvo ein wenic melwes (flour) vnd grobes brotes (bread) pfeffer
(pepper) oder ingeber (ginger) saltz (table salt) zvo mazze ein ey (chicken egg) oder zwey noch der
[159r] menge roeste daz wol zvo sammene snit zwei clueppelin eines vingers lanc als ein eln schaft
fornen sleht sinewel vnd nim des gesoten als groz als ein morche (morel) walkez sinewel in der hant
vnd fuege ez vmeme den spiz (skewer) als ein marach (morel) vnd zwengez vzzene daz ez krusp si legez
in ein pfannen (pan) laz ez sieden mit dem stecken (skewer) die wile daz siede so bewirke den andern
stecken (skewer) als du den einen vz nemest so lege den andern in . Vnd mache ir als vil als du wilt
wanne sie gar sin gesoten so nim sie vz ruere ein gehacketz muos (puree) mit butern (butter) daz
fuelle in die morchen (morel) vnd stecke sie entwerhes an den spiz (skewer) mache sie heiz vnde
betraufe sie mit butern (butter) vnd gib sie hin also mahtu auch machen morchen (morel) von hecheden
(northern pike) vnd von lehsen (salmon) vnd wo von du wilt .

condimente (sauce) dar veber vnd gib sie hin .

. Ein guot lecker spigerihtelin . Ach vnd versaltz nuer niht . Wanne ez ist ein guot geriht . Diz
ist ein guot lere von guoter spise

Mawrochen (morel) wildw machen mawrochen (morel) auf eyn plad (pancake) so nym kelbren lungen
(calf's lung) vnd dy wal vnd hack eyn ay (chicken egg) dar vnter vnd [272r] thu dar ein gut stupp
(spice) vnd gerib ens prot (bread) vnd hack es chlayn vnd mach eyn holcz daz zw pay den seyten
gespiczt sey vnd mitten gros als dy mawrochen (morel shaping tool) vnd streich der ful (stuffing)
dan an daz holcz (morel shaping tool) vmbeduem doch daz es albeg mitten gros sey vnd pach es dan in

henne-ban sede duckys wylle kylle, and hennes also hit wille spylle; and cast this to hom opon
grene; who wylle assay hit, o sothe may sene. <<6>> to make venegur manede; take a gad of stele i
wot in dede; in strong venegur ou schalt hit seke ix sythes in venegur, erof ou reke, a bere with e
hete hit ou may, and in goode wyne sleck hit i say; hit shalle be venegur i wot hit wele, to serve
at a tyme at fest or mele. And rosted benes, at steped han bene, goode wyne schalle turne to venegur
be dene. To preve venegur, we er hit be fyne. Ou take hys knyve or ellis myne, in harde drye flore a
hole to make; put in o venegur, i undurtake, if hit be good, welle, syr, hit schalle, yf hit be no 3
t, downe wylle hit falle. Is se 3 e i preved, so have i blys; erfore i wot at hit sothe is. To
powder befe with in a ny 3 t, ou welle o salt, in water bry 3 t; malt hit in bryne, set doun to
kele, put in y flesshe fayre and wele, and in a ny 3 t hit poudert schalle be, grene powdert orogh,
so mot i e. Yf y dysshe metes dere ben to salt, kerve a grene sod, i wot, ou schalt, and kover y pot
with o gresse done, o salt on o gresse shalle barke fulle sone. With y honde smyte of, i say; o salt
lay on anew ou may; ys schalt ou gedur hit, yche a dele, and make hit fresshe unto e mele. If i
schalle of ese potage spelle a whyle eron en most i dwelle; fyrste, to speke of furment , how hit is
made in yche degre. <<7>> furmente. Take wete, and pyke hit fayre [and clene] and do hit in a morter
shene; bray hit a lytelle, with water hit spryng tyl hit hulle, with-oute lesyng. En wyndo hit wele,
nede ou mot; wasshe hit fayre, put hit in pot; boyle hit tylle hit brest, en let hit doun, as i e
kenne. Take know mylke, and play hit up to hit be thykkerede to sup. Lye hit up with 3 olkes of
eyren, and kepe hit wele, lest hit berne. Coloure hit with safron and salt hit wele, and servyd
[servys?] hit forthe, syr, at e mele; with sugur candy, ou may hit dowce, if hit be served in grete
lordys howce. Take black sugur for mener menne; be ware er with, for hit wylle brenne. Amydone. Take
wete and stepe hit dayes ix; us chaunge y water yche day be dene. Brys hit in a morter ry 3 t
smalle, sethe hit with mylke and water with alle. Orowgh a herseve loke ou hit sye, and let hit
stonde and setel bye; poure oute e water, in clothe hit lay, tyl hit be drye ou turne hit ay. Ys is
a lycour as men sayn, er of i schalle speke more in playn. <<8>> conyngus in grav . Sethe welle y
conyngus in water clere, after, in water colde ou wasshe hom sere, take mylke of almondes, lay hit
anone with myed bred or amydone; fors hit with cloves or gode gyngere; boyle hit over o fyre, hew o
conyngus, do hom er to, seson hit with wyn or sugur o. Chekyns in cretene. Take cow mylke, lye hit
anone with flowre, or ellis with amydone; fors hit with galyngale and gode gyngere, with canel and
comyn, alle in fere, coloure hit with safron o; e chekyns by hom selfe o sethe er to, hew hom in
quarteres and lay hom inne, boyle hom up with alle, no more ne mynne; but seson hit with sugur
suete, and serve hom forthe for ay ben sete viande de cipur. Take braunne of capons or hennes ou
shalle; parboyle and drye hit with alle; hew hom smalle, bray in mortere, as smalle as bred, at myed
were; take good almonde mylke anone and lye hit up with amydone or with floure of ryse, ou may;
coloure hit with safron, i e say; boyle hit after yche adele, charge hit with flesshe brayed wele;
<<9>> seson hit with sugur and en y dysshe with almondes set ou schalle florysshe. Mortrews de
chare. Take hennes and fresshe porke, y e kenne, sethe hom togedur alwayes enne; take hem up, pyke
out e bonys, enbande e porke, syr, for o nonys; hew hit smalle and grynde hit wele, cast it agayne,
so have ou cele, in to e brothe, and charge hit enne with myed wastelle, as i e kenne; colour hit
with safron, at at tyde; boyle hit and set hit doune be syde; lye hit with 3 olkes of eren ry 3 t,
and florysshe y dysshe with pouder ou my 3 t. Blonc manger. Take ryse and loke ou wasshe hom clene,
and orowgh a strynour ou hom strene; temper hom with almonde mylke anon. Take brawne of capons or
henne good won, tese hit smalle, as i e lere; do e ryse in o mylke over e fyre, let hit boyle for
ony nede; charge hit with tesyd flesshe in dede; seson hit with sugar, and floresshe with fryud
almondes o lordes dysshe. Andon for wylde digges, swannus, and piggus. Take, wasshe o isues of
swannes anon, and skoure o guttus with salt ichon; <<10>> sethe alle to gedur and hew hit smalle. E
flesshe and eke o guttus with alle; take galingale and gode gyngere and canel, and grynd hom al in
fere; and myude bred ou take erto, and temper hit up with brothe also; coloure hit with brend bred
or with blode, seson hit with venegur, a lytelle for gode; welle alle togedur in a posnet; in
service forthe ou schalt hit sett. Nombuls. Take o hert and o mydruv and e kydnere, and hew hom
smalle, as i e lere; presse oute e blode, wasshe hom ou schalle, sethe hom in water and in gode ale;
coloure hit with brende bred or with blode; fors hit with peper and canel gode, sett hit to o fyre,
as i e telle in tale; kele hit with a litelle ale, and set hit downe to serve in sale. Ano er maner
for noumbuls. Take e noumbuls of e veneson, in water and salt o wasshe hom sone, and in twynne
waters, ou schalt hom sethe; grynd bred and peper with ale full smethe, with e secunde brothe ou
temper hit mun, and hew y noumbuls alle and sum; and boyle y sew, do hom er inne, of ys mater er, no
more ne myn. <<11>> charlet. Take swettest mylke, at ou may have, colour hit with safron, so god e
save; take fresshe porke and sethe hit wele, and hew hit smalle every dele; swyng eyryn, and do er
to; set hit over e fyre, enne boyle hit and sture lest hit brenne; whenne hit welles up, ou schalt
hit kele with a litel ale, so have ou cele; when hit is ino 3 e, ou sett hit doune, and kepe hit
lest hit be to broune. For charlet icoloured. Take almondes unblanchyd, wasshe hom and grynd; temper
hom with rede wyne, at is so kynd; alye hit up with floure of ryce, do er to pynys and saunders for
spyce, for to coloure hit, loke ou do is, and o er goode spyces ou take, iwys, bothe strong and
swete ou do er to; salt hit, boyle hit, sethe hit forthe o, with annes icomfet, florysshe hit ou
schalle; messe hit in dysshes to be served in halle. Iusselle. Take myud bred, and eyren ou swynge;
do hom togeder with out lettyng, take fresshe broth of gode befe, coloure hit with safron, at is me
lefe, boyle hit softly, and in o boylyng, do er to sage and persely 3 oyng. <<12>> breuet de
almonde. Take gode almonde mylke anon, and loke ou lye hit with amydone, or with flowre at is bake;
coloure hit with safron, i undurtake; fors hit with powder of y male of gyngere, canel, and
galingale. Take pertrykes and chykyns and hom wele sethe; [12/1] hew hom in quarters fayre and
smethe; do at mylke over o fyre at tyde, and boyle and sett hit doune besyde, and florysshe hit with
powdur, as i e kenne, ou may have more menske emong alle menne. Blonk desore. Take ryse and wasshe
hom in a cup, grynd hom smalle and temper up with almonde mylke, so have ou cele; do hit over o fyre
and boyle hit wele; take braune of capons or hennes alle, hew hit at hit be ri 3 t smalle; and grynd
hit wele, as myud brede, and do er to, as i e rede; seson hit with sugur grete plente, with fryid
almondes florysshe so fre. Bucnade. Take almonde mylke as i con preche; coloure hit with safron as i
e teche; fors hit with poudur, at is gode; take larde of porke, wele so yn, by o rode; hew hit in
gobettes wele afyne; loke ey ben smale and put hem inne; <<13>> lye hit with floure or amydone,
boyle hit wele and sett hit done; florysshe hit with powdur, as i e kenne, enne may hit be served,
before gode men. Rose. Take flour of ryse, as whyte as sylke, and hit welle, with almond mylke;
boyle hit tyl hit be chargyd, enne take braune of capone or elle of henne; loke ou grynd hit wondur
smalle, and sithen ou charge hit with alle; coloure with alkenet, sawnder, or ellys with blode, fors
hit with clowes or macys gode; seson hit with sugur grete plent , is is a rose, as kokes telle me.
Lede lardes [leche lardes]. Take eyren and swete mylke of a cow, swyng hom togedur, as i byd now;
take larde of fresshe porke with alle, sethe hit and schere hit on peses smalle; cast er in and
boyle hit, enne styr hit wele, as i e kenne, tyl hit be gedered on crud harde; leche hit, and rost
hit afterwarde apone a gredel, en serve ou may hit forthe, with spit, as i e say. For blanchyd
mortrews. Sethe hennes and porke, at is fulle fresshe; bray almondes unblanchyd and temper hom
nesshe with clene brothe, and drawe hom o; <<14>> alay y flesshe smalle grounden to, and floure of
ryce ou grynd also; cast powder of gyngere and sugur erinne, but loke at hit be not to yn, but
stondand and saltid mesurl and kepe y dysshe mete for o maystr . Peions istued. Take peions and hew
hom in morselle smalle, put hom in a er yn pot, ou shalle; take pilled garlek and herbys anon, hack
hom smalle er ou more don; put hom in o pot, and er to take gode brothe with wyte grece, ou no 3 t
forsake; do powdur er to and gode verius, coloure hit with safron, and salt inow; ou put in pote ese
ynges alle, and stue y peions us ou schalle. Sowpus dorre. Take almondes, bray hem, wryng hom up;
boyle hom with wyn rede to sup; en temper hom with wyn, salt, i rede, and loke ou tost fyne wete
brede, and lay in dysshes, dubene with wyne; do in is dysshes mete, at is so fyne; messe hit forthe,
and florysshe hit enne with sugur and gynger, as i e kenne. Gruel of almondes. Take almondes
unblanchid and bray hom sone, put ote mele to, enne hase ou done, and grynde alle sammen, and draw
hit enne with water and sethe, as i e kenne; <<15>> coloure hit with safron and salt hit enne, and
set in sale byfore gode menne. Ioutus de almonde. Take erbe, perboyle hom, fayre and wele; hew hom
and grynde hom every dele; take almondes unblanched and grynd hom smalle, draw 3 e hom with water, i
wote ou schalle; set hit over e fyre, yn erbis ou sethe with o mylke forsayde, at grounden is
smethe; cast erto sugur, and salt anone; take er y ioutes made dalmone. Caudel dalmone. Take
almondes unblanchyd and hom ou bray; drawe hom up with wyn, i dar wele say; er to do pouder of good
gyngere and sugur, and boyle alle ese in fere, and coloure hit with safron and salt hit wele, and
serve hit forthe sir at o mele. Buttur of almonde mylke. Take thykke mylke of almondes clere, boyle
wele alle in fere; and in o boylyng, cast erinne venegur, o er ellys gode wyne; do hit so enne in a
canvas enne, in so un, gar hit on hepe to renne; in clothe ou henge hit a myle way, and after in
colde water ou hit lay; serve hit forthe in e dysshe, at day o lorde is servyd with fysshe. <<16>>
ryse. Take ryse and wasshe and grynde hem smalle, temper hom with almonde mylke ou schalle; drau 3 e
hom thorowghe a streynour clene, boyle hom and seson hom with sugur schene; fors hit with fryude
almondes gode, en hase ou done, syr, by o rode. Kaudel ferry. Take almondes unblanchyd, so have ou
cele, and wasshe hom fayre and grynd hom wele; temper hom up with wyne so clene, and drau 3 e hom
orowgh a canvas shene; in pot ou coloure hit with safron, and lye hit up with amydone, or with
floure of ryse so fre; ry 3 t thykke loke ou at be; seson hit with sugur grete plent , florysshe hit
with maces, i tel e. For to make a rape. Take raysyns of corauns erto, and wyte wynne ou take also;
sethe enne o er raysyns grete in rede wyne, and boyle a lytul with hete; do opon a broche, rost hom
bydene a lytel, and take hom fayre and clene and bray hom in a morter smalle, a crust of brede ou
bray with alle. Put alle in e pot with grythe, o raysyns of corauns, o swete wyne with, a lytul
vengur, and pouder take o of clowes, maces and quibibis to; <<17>> boyle alle to geder, and serve
hit enne, and sett hit forthe before goode men. Mylke rostyd. Take swete mylke and put in panne,
swyng eyren with alle, grynde safron and do erto; welle hit enne, tylle hit wax thykke, as i e
kenne; and sethe and sye hit thorowghe a cloth, presse hit, at leves, withouten othe; when hit is
colde, leche hit with knyves; rost hit, and messe hit forthe on schyves. For to make a potage of
welkes. Take welkes and wasshe fayre, in blythe, in water, and take whyte salt erwith and after
hakke hom on a borde, as smalle as ou may, at a worde, and bray hom in a morter clere; sethe hom in
mylke over e fyre; of almondes or of a clow ou take schalle, lye hit with amydone erwith alle;
coloure hit with safrone, and do erinne poudur of peper, or goode comyne. For to make potage of
oysturs. Perboyle yn oysturs and take hom oute; kepe welle y bre with outen doute, and hakke hom on
a borde full smalle, and bray in a morter ou schalle; do hom in hor owne brothe for goode, do mylke
of almondes er to by e rode, and lye hit up with amydone, and frye smalle mynsud onyone <<18>> in
oyle, or sethe hom in mylke ou schalle; do powdur erto of spyces withalle, and coloure hit enne with
safron gode; hit is holden restoratyf fode. Sauge seynes. Take swynes fete and sethe hom clene, take
3 olkes of eyren at harde bene, and sage as mykul as fall erto, gode powdur, and temper with
venegur; when ou hase so yn o fete ry 3 t welle, clovyn hom and paryd hom er tylle, lay hom on
dysshe with blythe, o sawce on e 3 olkes erwyth. For to make a compost. Take o chekyns and hew hom
for o seke, all but e hede and e legges eke; take a handfulle of herb lovache, and ano er of
persely, als of sage at never was founde fals, and no er of lekes and alle hom wasshe ose herbes in
water, at rennes so rasshe; breke orowghe y honde, bothe herbe and leke, with a pynt of hony enbeny
hom eke, summe of ese herbes ou shalle laye in e pottus bothun [sothun?], as i e say; summe of e
chekyns ou put erto, and en of e herb 3 do to also; so of o ton so of at o er, o herb 3 on e last my
dere brother; above ese herbus a lytul larde smalle myncyd, haldand togeder warde; take powder of
gynger and canel god wone, cast on ese o er thynges everychon; <<19>> be sle 3 e and powre in water
enne to myd o pot, as i the kenne; opone o bruys poure hit withinne, and cover hit at no hete oute
wynne, and tendurly seyth hit ou do may, salt hit, serve hit, as i e say. Blanc maungere of fysshe.
Take a pownde of ryse and sethe hom wele, tyl at ay brostene; and lete hom kele. Mylke of almondes
erto ou cast, o tenche or lampray do to on last; welle alle togeder, as i e kenne, and messe hit
forthe before godde men. Mortrews of fysshe. Take o kelkes of fysshe anon, and o lyver of o fysshe,
sethe hom alon; en take brede and peper and ale, and temper o brothe fulle welle ou schalle, and
welle hit togeder and serve hit enne, and set in sale before good mene. For to make rose dalmoyne.
Take whyte pese and wasshe hom wele, tylle at ey hulle, sethe yche adele, and bene clene of am, en
schalle ou caste in to o pot and cover in hast; and loke no brethe er passe oute, but boyle hom wele
with owtyn dowte; of almonde mylke ou kest erto, of floure of ryse and salt also; <<20>> coloure hit
with safrone and messe hit, enne set hit in sale before goode men. For a kolys. E brawne take of
sothun henne or chekyne, and hew hit smalle and bray en with wyne, with ote grotis, and whyte brede
eke; with e brothe of henne ou tempur hit meke; take oute e bonys and grynd hit smalle, in to e
brothe ou kast hit alle, and sye hit thurgh a clothe clene; dose hit, and serve hit forthe bydene.
Gruel of porke. Take brawne of swyne, perboyle hit wele, and grynde hit smalle, syr, everydele; with
3 olkes of eyren ou schalle hit lye, set hit over e fyre for- ye, put whyte grece erto, bewar, iwys,
let hit not sethe lest ou mys. Do er to powder and safron enne and messe hit forthe before goode
menne; powder dowce eron ou kast stondande at dressore on e last. Conyngus in cyne. [>cyve.] smyte e
conyngus in pese smalle; and sethe hom in brothe gode ou shalle; mynsyn onyons in grece ou sethe,
and in good brothe, at is so smethe walle togeder; and drau 3 e alioure of blode and brede sumdele
sowre, <<21>> sesonut with venegur and good brothe eke, kast salt erto and powder fulle meke. Harus
in cyne. [>cyve.] perboyle e hare and larde hit wele, sethyn loke ou rost hir everydele; take onyons
and loke ou hew hom smalle, frye hom in grece, take peper and ale, and grynde togeder o onyons also;
coloure hit with safrone and welle hit o; lay e hare in charioure, as i e kenne; powre on e sewe and
serve hit enne. Harus in a sewe. Alle rawe o hare schalle hacked be, in gobettis smalle, syr, levys
me; in hir owne blode seyn or sylud clene, grynde brede and peper withalle bydene; enne temper hit
with e same bre, enne boyled and salted hit servyd schalle be. Harus in abrotet.
[>harus_in_a_browet.] hew smalle y hare in gobetus gode, sethe hom in brothe with alle his blode;
when hit is so un wondur wele, draw 3 h thurgh a streynour, so have ou cele; take almondes
unblanchid, wasshe hom and grynde; with self brothe temper hom by kynde; take onyons and perboyle
hom ou mot, and dresshe hom smalle, kest hom in pot with alle o er thyngus, and cast er to with
venegur and salt, en hase ou doo. <<22>> harus in perdoylyse. Take harys and perboyle hom, i rede,
in goode brothe, kele hit for drede, and hew y flesshe and cast erinne. Take swongen eggus, no more
ne myn, and cast in y sewe and sethe hit enne. Take obles and wafrons, as i e kenne, close hom in
dysshes fare and wele; salt e sewe, so have ou cele, and lay hit above as gode men done, and messe
hit forthe, syr, at o none. Hennes in brewes. With porke ou sethe o henne fatte, grynde brede and
peper and be not batte; and comyne also ou schalle grynde, seson hom with ale, at is hor kynde; with
o brothe of hennes ou temper hit shalle, boyle hit, coloure hit, salt hit withalle; serve hom
forthe, as ou may see, ese er hennes in browet, levys ou me. Chekyns in browet. Take chekyns, scalde
hom fayre and clene; take persole, sauge, o er herb 3 , grene grapus, and stope y chekyns with
wynne; take goode brothe, sethe hom erinne, so at ay sone boyled may be; coloure e brothe with
safrone fre, and cast eron powder dowce, for to be served in goode mennys howse. <<23>> chekyns in
cawdel. In brothe ou boyle y chekyns gode; take 3 olkes of eyren, syr, for o rode, alye hom up with
brothe forsayde; take powder gynger, abrayde, and sugur, and rew, and safron clere, and salt, and
set hit over o fyre; with owtyn boylyng messe hit forthe enne; y chekyns hole take, i e kenne, of
[yf?_ m ] ay be brokyn, on dysshe hom lay, helde hom e sewe, as i e say. For to boyle fesawantes and
pertryks. Take goode brothe, erin ou pyt y fesauntes and y pertryks, at men may wyt. Do erto ale,
floure, peper fre, of hole canel, good quantit ; and let alle sethe erwyth fulle wele, and messe hit
forthe, syr, at e mele. Powder dowce erin ou cast, when hit [is] servyd on e last. Roo in a sewe.
Take o roo, pyke hit clene forthy; boyle hit ou shalt and after hit drye; hew hit on gobettis, at
ben smalle, do hit in pot withalle; kest wyn erto, if ou do ry 3 t, take persole and sawge and ysope
bry 3 t, wasshe hom and hew hom wondur smalle, and do erto hit ou schalle, coloure hit with blode or
sawnders hors. <<24>> hennes in grav . Take hennes and rost, as i e kenne, sithinn, hew hom smalle
and frye hom; enne take wyne or peper or venegur to, grynd hit togeder with hennes o; lye hit with 3
olkes of eyren wele, coloure hit with safrone everydele, and messe hit forthe withoutene ony more,
and loke ou for 3 ete no 3 t ys lore. Capons in covisye. Take capons and sethe hom wele, and hew hom
smalle ilkadele; take peper and brede, and grynde hit smalle, and temper hit up with capon alle;
take why 3 te of eyren harde so un o, and hake hom smalle and do erto, and boyle e capon and coloure
hit enne with safrone, and do as i kenne; o 3 olkes of eggus, i telle e, alle hole ou put in disshe
so fre. Hennes in gauncel. Take first and rost welle y henne, take garlek by hit selfe and grynd;
enne blonde hit with mylke and put alle in panne, and hew yn henne and do er to enne y henne and 3
olkes of eyren imelle; coloure hit with safron and let hit welle, and messe hit forthe, i telle e;
but ou wille alye hit with floure so fre. <<25>> lamprayes in browet. Take lamprayes and scalde hom
by kynde, sythyn, rost hom on gredyl, and grynde peper and safrone; welle hit with alle, do o
lampreyes and serve hit in sale. Lamprayes in galentine. Take lamprayes and hom let blode at o
navel, and scalde hom for gode; rost hom enne, and ou hom laye alle hole in platere, as i e saye;
serve with galentine, made in sale, with gyngere, canel and galingale. For tenchis in grav . Sethe y
tenchis, and after hom brede, and rost hom on a gredel, i rede; grynd peper and safron with ale, i
kenne, with tenchis brothe, ou temper hit; enne lay o tenche opon a platere fayre, do on at browet
withouten disware. Chawdewyne de boyce. Take smalle notes, schale not [out?_ m ] kurnele, as ou dose
of almondes, fayre and wele; frye hom in oyle, en sethe hom ry 3 t in almonde mylke at is bry 3 t;
en ou schalle do in floure of ryce and also o er pouder of spyce; fry o er curneles besyde also,
coloure ou hit with safron, or ou fer goo, to divers o mete ou schalt hit set, with o fryed curnels
with outen let. <<26>> capons in cassolyce. Take capons and schalde and pyke hom en; e skyn ou opon,
as i e kenne, be hynde o hede, blaw hym with penne; enne ryses o skyn before, rayse up o skyn alle
hole abowte, take porke and hen flesshe with outen doute, and 3 olkes of eyren and gode powder; of
alle o thynges ou make farsure, and farse o skyn and perboyle hit wele; en larde o capone, rost hym
yche dele; of almonde mylke and amydone make bater, and coloure hit anone with safron; serve hit at
fyre rostande, enbene hit wele withe y ry 3 t honde. For to make momene. Take whyte wyne, i telle e,
and sugur erto ry 3 t grete plent ; take, bray o brawne of a 3 t capon; to a pot of oyle of on
galon, and of hony a qwharte ou take; do hit er to as ever ou wake, take powder o mountenaunce of a
pownde, and galingale ginger and canel rownde, and cast er to, and styre hit; enne alle in on pot
sethe hit, i kenne. Lange de beof. Take o ox tonge and schalle hit wele, sethe hit, broche hit in
larde yche dele, with cloves of gelofer hit broch ou shalle, en do hit to fyre and rost hit alle;
<<27>> with 3 olkes of eyren enbene hit ay whille at hit rostes, as i e say. En take blode, at is so
lefe, welle hit in fresshe brothe of e befe, bray hit fulle wele in on mortere, do in fayre grece,
at is so clere; fors hit with spicys ry 3 t gode with alle, and sythun, serve hit in to e halle; to
e forsayde tonge is sawce is dy 3 t, here endes oure potage fulle gode ry 3 t. Pro salsamentis. --
to make sawce. Now speke i wylle of sauces sere: how ay ar made, i wylle 3 ow lere, next after
potage ay servyd schalle be, as i have lurned in ys cuntr . Pur verde sawce. Take persole, peletre
an oyns, and grynde, take whyte bred myude by kynde, temper alle up with venegur or wyne, force hit
with powder of peper fyne. Sawce for mawdelardes rosted. Take onyons and hew hom wele, put sum in o
mawdelarde, so have ou cele, and hacke mo onyons, as i e kenne; with o grece of o mawdelarde ou
sethe hom, en take ale, mustarde and hony o, boyle alle togeder or ou more do; for maularde rosted
ys sawce is dy 3 t, and served in sale by gode ry 3 t. <<28>> sawce for vele and venysone. Take
brede and frye hit in grece ou schalle, with brothe of venegur draw 3 e hit withalle, kast powder of
gynger anon er to and peper, and sethe o and messe hit forthe; a sawce hit is for vele and venyson,
iwys. Blaunche sawce for capons. Take blanchid almondis and smal hom grynde, temper hom with verius,
at is hor kynde, powder of gynger, and kast er to, and messe hit forthe, en hase ou do. Sawce best
for capons rostyd. Take lyver of capons and rost hom wele, take annes and grynd hit, as have ou
cele, pare gynger and canel gode er to, a lytel crust of brede ou take also; grynde al ese ynges
wondur smalle, with verius temper hom up ou schalle; with grece of capons boyle hit in sy 3 t and
serve hit forthe fulle wele ou my 3 t. Sawce sirer for mawdelardus. Take brede and blode iboylyd and
grynde, and draw 3 he hit orowghe a clothe by kynde, with venegur gode and sesounabulle, with powder
of gynger, and peper abulle, and grece of mawdelarde; and boyle alle wele, and messe hit forthe syr
at o mele. <<29>> gawncel for e gose. Take garlek and grynde hit wele for y, temper hit with water a
lytel, perdy; put floure er to and also salt, colour hit with safron i wot ou schalt; temper hit up
with cow-mylke o, and sethe hit and serve hit forthe also. Sawce for swannus. Take o offal and o
lyver of o swan, in gode brothe ou sethe hom an; when hit is sothyne, take oute e bonus, smalle hew
o flesshe, syr, for e nonus; make alyoure of crust of brede, of blode of swanne, at so un is lede,
caste powdur of gynger and clawes er to, of peper and wyn ou take also, and salt hit en and sethe
hit wele; cast in y flesshe, hewen yche a dele, and messe hit forthe, as i e kenne, set hit in sale
before goode menne. [sawce] for cranys and herons. The crane is enarmed ful wele i wot with larde of
porke at on bare mot, rostyd and eten with gode gingere, at is o sawce at servis ere; o heroun is
rosted, as have i blys, and eton with gynger as his kynde is. [sawce] for pekokys and pertrikis.
Pekokys and pertrikys perboylyd schyn be, lardyd, rostyd, eton, levys me, <<30>> with gyngere,
payndmayn paryd clene and groundyn in a morter, at is schene, temperid up with venegur gode, with
powder of gyngere and salt, by o rode, and draw 3 en orowghe a streynour mylde, servid forthe with
pekok and pertrik wylde. Galentyne. Take crust of brede and grynde hit smalle, take powder of
galingale and temper with alle powder of gyngere and salt also; temper hit with venegur er ou more
do, draw 3 e hit urughe a streynour enne, and messe hit forthe before gode menne. Sawce camelyne,
kervelettes and o er thyngus. Take raysons of corouns and kyrnels smalle of notes, and do away o
schale, take crust of brede and clowe in fere, and powder imaked of gode gyngere, flowre of canel ou
schalle take, enne bray alle togedur, as i e kenne, in a morter and salt erto; temper alle with
venegur, en hase ou do, and messe hit forthe; is is sawce fyne, at men calles camelyne. For
lumbardus mustard. Take mustarde and let hit drye anonyn, sir, wyturlye; stomper hit in a morter
fyne, and fars hit urghe a clothe of lyne; do wyne erto and venegur gode, sture hom wele togeder for
e rode, <<31>> and make hit yke inowghe enne, whenne ou hit spendes byfore gode menne, and make hit
thynne with wyne, i say, with diverse metes ou serve hit may. For pykulle. Take droppyng of capone
rostyd wele with wyne and mustarde, as have ou cele, with onyons smalle schrad and sothun in grece,
meng alle in fere and forthe hit messe. Filetus in galentine. Take filetes of porke and half hom
rost, smyte hom in peses with outene bost; draw 3 e a lyoure of blode and brede withalle, do venegur
er to, i wot ou schalle; fors hit with powder of canel, or gode gynger, sethe hit with o flesshe,
alle in fere; salt and messe forthe, enne set hit in sale before gode menne. Pigges in sawce. Take
pigges and scalde hom in water clene, sethe hom in water and salt bydene; take hom up and lete hom
kele; take persoley and sage, and grynde hit wele with e brothe of pigges with owtene rewarde, and 3
olkes of eggus at so un ar harde, temper alle with venegur sumdele stondande; lay pigges in a
vessayle, with bothe hande, held y sawce a-bofe tolde [cold_ms.] for y, and serve hit alle forthe,
syr, wyturly. <<32>> sawce madame. Take sawge, persoly, ysope, saveray, onyons gode, peres, garlek,
i say, and grapes; go fille y gose enne and sew y hole, no grece oute renne; lay hur to fyre and
rost hyr browne, and kepe o grece at falles doune. Take galingale and o grece at renne, do hit in
posnet, as i e kenne; whenne o gose is rostyd, take hir away, smyte hir in pesys, i e pray; at is
within, ou schalle take oute, kest in y posnet with outene doute; 3 if hit is thyke do erto wyne,
and powder of galingale at is fyne, and powder dowce and salt also; boyle alle togeder er ou fyr go,
in a dysshe y gose ou close e sawce abofe, as i suppose. Gose in a hogge pot. In pesis ou schalle y
gose stryke, take water and wyne bothe ilyke; do in y gose; and onyons ou take a gode quantit , as i
er spake, and erbus hacked ou take also, and cast ou in er ou more do; en set y pot over o fyre, and
hit wele stir for e hyre; and make a lyoure of brede and blode, and lye hit erwithe, for hit is
gode; kast powder erto and salt anon, and messe hit, enne ou hase done. <<33>> to save venysone
fresshe over e 3 er. Yf ou wylle kepe e tayle of a dere fresshe in seson over o 3 ere, or o er
venesone yf at hit nede, us schalt u do, i wot in dede; presse out o blode, for anythyng at is cause
for grete rotyng; in er yne pot ou shalt hit pyt and feyre hony do into hit; to o hony stonde over o
flesshe too fyngurs thyke for harde or nesshe; with leder o mouthe en schalt ou bynde, kepe hit fro
ayre, son or wynde, in cofer, or huche or seler merke. For to save venysone fro restyng. Take
venesone when hit is new slayn, and cover hit alle with ferne playn at no wynde enter er to; and
whenne ou hast covered hit so, lede hit home, selor hit lay at wynde ne sone ne ughe hit may; dresse
hit wele and wassh hit clene, sythen, lay hit in water alle by dene, er in be half a day to lye;
enne take hit oute on flore to drye, enne after take salt a quantit ; boyle hit in clene water so
fre, and kele hit, at he be bot lue, and erin wasshe y venesone true, and let hit lye erin thre
dayes and thre ny 3 htes, by any kyns wayes; then take hit oute of at water, salt hit wyth drye
salt, alle in fere. <<34>> and do hit in a barel enne; e barel staf ful as i e kenne, stop wele o
hede for wynde and sone, for hit wylle payre o venysone. To keep herb 3 over e wyntur. Take floure
and rere o cofyns fyne, wele stondande withouten stine; take tenderons of sauge with owte lesyng,
and stop one fulle up to o ryng; enne close o lyd fayre and wele, at ayre go not oute never a dele,
do so with saveray, percil and rewe; and enne bake hom harde, wel ne 3 e brende; sythun, kepe hom
drye and to hom tent; is powder schalle be of more vertu, en opone er e when hit gru. For lyoure
best. Take drye floure, in cofyne hit close, and bake hit hard, as i suppose; ou may hit kepe alle
ys fyve 3 ere, ere-with alye mony metes sere; here endys oure sawce, at i foretolde. De cibis
assatis. Of rostyd mete now speke i wolde, for er bene bestes at schyne be rost, as conyng, pigges,
ful wele ou wost, and foules also at rostyd schyne be on diverse manere in her degr ; and kostyf of
motone, at i wele knaw, enbrochyd shal be, by ry 3 t gode law; <<35>> and also fysshe ou schalle
enbroche, as porpays at swymmes by o see roche; erfore i telle 3 ou now, i rede, what schalle rost
with neck and hede. For e crane. O crane schalle fyrst enarmed be, scalde and pulde ful warl , dra 3
un at o syde as wodcockis, with legges al hole he rostyd is; abowte o brothe o necke ou cralle, put
in o bylle at coler ou schalle; enarme hym forthe as hit is tolde before, and serve ys crane bolde.
For heroun rostyd. E heroun is slayn, as have i sene; e herte oute pyke alle bydene, under e lyft
wyng o neck bone steke, devoyded, as men me tolde meke; enne under o wynge o skyn ou cralle, pyt in
o bylle at coler ou schalle. For wodcock, sny 3 t and curlue. To wodcok, snype, curlue also, e
betore in fere with hom schalle goo; alle schun be dra 3 un, syr, at o syde, and honestly rostyd
with outene pryde, with neck and hede suande in fere, o bylle put urghe o e 3 es sere; on alle ese
fowles o legges schune bene, summe cralled, sum stre 3 t, as i have sene. And gret as heroun rostyd
schalle be, at a kny 3 t is called for gentlor , <<36>> a capone also at comyn is, o pecok wyth his
tayle so have i blys, o fesaunt kok, but not o henne; us have i lurnet at gentil men; alle o er
foles at swymmen in flode, at schun be rostyd, syr, by o rode, with outen necke or hede, i trowe,
and o er smalle bryddes, at i wele knaw, as osel, smityng, laveroc gray, pertryk, werkock, i dayr
wele say; o kormorount schalle rost iwys, with o bylle opone for grete koyntes. For pygges farsyd.
Take swongen eyrene and floure er to, and powder of peper er ou more do; blend alle togeder and salt
erwith; coloure hit with safrone, so have ou blythe; put alle in body of o pygge, rost hit on broche
of irne bygge enfarsed; o cle of pygge schalle be festened in e cheke so mot ou e; o hender legges
enoynt ou schalle, o cles by o sydes ou festun withalle. For fraunche mele. Take swongene eyrene in
bassyne clene, and kreme of mylke at is so schene, and myyd bred, ou put er to, and powder of peper
er ou more do; coloure hit with safrone in hast, and kremelyd sewet of schepe on last, and fylle y
bagge at is so gode, and sew hit fast, syr, for o rode; <<37>> whenne hit is so un, ou schalt hit
leche, and broyle hyt on gredel, as i e teche. For bours. Take porke and gese, hew hom ou schalle on
gobetes, with powder of peper withalle; hom sethe in pot at is so clene, with oute any water, with
salt, i wene; fro martyn messe to gode tyde evyne, ys mete wylle serve, ou may me lene, at dyner or
soper, if at hit nede; ou take gode ale, at is not quede, er in ou boyle o forsayde mete o more
worship ou may gete. For powme dorrys. Take porke and grynde hit rawe, i kenne, temper hit with
swongen egges; enne kast powder to make hit on a balle; in playand water ou kast hit schalle to
harden, enne up ou take, enbroche hit fayre for goddes sake. Endore hit with 3 olkes of egges en
with a fedyr at fyre, as i e kenne; bothe grene and rede ow may hit make with iuse of herb 3 i
undertake; halde under a dysshe at no 3 t be lost, more honest hit is as ou wele wost. Hasteletes on
fysshe day. Take fyggus quartle, and raysyns, o hole dates, almondes, rine hom also on broche of
irne, and rost hom sone; endore hom with 3 olkes of egges anone. <<38>> here endys oure hastere at i
of spake; to speke of bakun mete i wolde clake, for lamprays, darials and flaunes also, and o er
metes mony and moo. For lamprays bakun. Fyrst scalde y lamprays fayre and wele, as i tolde byfore,
so have ou cele; so un, rere a cofyne of flowre so fre, rolle in o lampray, as hit may be; take
mynsud onyons er to, gode wonne, but fyrst take powder of peper, anon of maces, cloves and graynys
also, and dates al hole ou take erto, poure rede wyne erto ou schalle, coloure hit with safrone and
closen alle. In myddes o lydde an tuel ou make, set hit in o ovyn for to bake; 3 ete take hit oute,
fede hit with wyne, lay on o tuel a past fulle fyne, and bake hit forthe, as i e kenne, to serve in
sale before gode menne. For darials. Take creme of almonde mylke iwys, and 3 olkes of eyren, so have
ou blys, and make a batere at is ful gode, and rere a cofyne with mylde mode; and sethe a
mawdelarde, at fat is enne, and cut in peses, as i e kenne; square as dises ou shalt hit make, kast
hit in batere, and powder ou take of gynger, of kanel, at gode is, o enfors hit wele er ou more do,
<<39>> and loke y cofyne be hardened wele, powre in y batere, so have ou cele, with a disshe hit
florysshe ou may, with blanchyd almondes, as i e say. For flaunes. Take new chese and grynde hit
fayre, in morter with egges, with out dysware; put powder er to of sugur, i say, coloure hit with
safrone ful wele ou may; put hit in cofyns at bene fayre, and bake hit forthe, i e pray. For
custanes. Grynde porke, brek eyren er to anon, with powder of peper er ou more done; put hit in
cofyn, at harde is bake, and 3 olke of egge en shalt ou take, that harde is so un, lay in to o top
as hit were a gyldene knop. For risshens. Take grounden porke at so un hase bene with peper and
swongen egges clene; put berme er to, i undertake, as tome as belle hit wille hit make; lay hit in a
roller as sparlyng fysshe, frye hit in grece, lay hit in dysshe. For freture. With egges and floure
in batere ou make, put berme er to, i undertake; <<40>> coloure hit with safrone er ou more do; take
powder of peper and cast er to, kerve appuls overtwert and cast erin, frye hom in grece, no more ne
mynne. Crustate of flesshe. Take peiuns and smalle chekuns with alle and o er smale bryddes, and hew
hom smalle; and sethe hom alle togedur oo in brothe and in white grece, also in verius, and do er to
safroune; fyrst make a fole trap ou mun, pynche hym, cowche hym y flesshe erby; kast erin raysyns of
corouns forthy, and powder dowce and salt gode won; breke eyren and streyne hom thorowghe a clothe
anone, and swyng y sewe erwyth enne, and helde hit onne e flesshe i kenne, and kover y trap and hele
hit wele, and serve hit forthe, syr, at e mele. Loysyns. In erthen pot put brothe for hast; take
floure of payndemayn, and make y past with water, er of y fele ou make with a roller, and drye hit,
i undurtake a 3 ayne o sonne at hit be harde; kast erin brothe and make rewarde; to sethe hom take
rawe chese anone and grate hit in disshes mony on with powder dowce; and lay er in y loseyns abofe e
chese with wynne, and powder on last spryngil hit ou may; ose loysyns er harde to make in fay.
<<41>> tartlotes. Take porke sothun, and grynde hit wele with safroune, and medel hit ylkadel with
egges and raysyns of corouns; o take powder and salt, and do erto; make a fole of doghe, and close
is fast, this flesshe at hewene was open o last kover hit with lyddes, and pynche hit fayre, korven
in e myddes two loyseyns a payr, set hit with fryed almondes sere, and coloure e past with safroune
dere, and bake hit forthe, as i e kenne, and set in sale before gode menne. Chewetes on fysshe day.
